Delibird Presents has different stock depending on the location. Here are the items exclusive to the Cascarrafa Store.

Cascaraffa’s Gym is right at the top of the city, and you’ll have to take the elevators to get there. However, as you approach the entrance, one of the Gym staff will approach you and tell you that the Gym Leader Kofu has gone shopping, but he left his wallet behind. His assistant asks you to take his wallet to him. Say yes and you’ll be directed to Porto Marinada where the market is.

The easiest way to get here is through the Asado Desert . With our new high jump power it’s easy to jump to the bottom of the city and into the desert. Kofu is a Water-type Gym Leader, and there are some Cacnea in the desert if you need something to deal Super Effective damage. There are also level 40 Pokémon in the desert so be careful what you run into. They will be difficult to catch and won’t obey you until you have Kofu’s badge anyway.

If you go through the desert you might go close to the Quaking Earth Titan triggering Arven ’s call. Don’t worry if you do, he’ll wait until you’re ready to take it on, so you can keep heading to Porto Marinada. There is a Pokémon Center as you go down into the town so make sure you trigger it before you go in. The market where Kofu is lies right in the center of town.

Before you approach Kofu at the market, make sure that your Pokémon are healed and you have an Electric - or Grass-type in your lead. As soon as you approach Kofu, Gym Trainer Hugo will battle you. He leads with his Floatzel that likes to use Aqua Jet so your speed doesn’t matter too much. By comparison his Clauncher is a lot easier to deal with.

Once you beat Hugo, Kofu will approach you and thank you for returning his wallet. Kofu will then give you 50,000 Poké Dollars and ask you to bid on some seaweed for him, telling you that you can keep the change. It will always go for less than 50,000 Poké Dollars but exactly how much money you receive is random. Just make sure that you bid and you’ll pass the task.
Once you hand the seaweed over to Kofu you will have passed the Gym Test you can fly back to Cascarrafa to go to the Gym and challenge Kofu himself.

As your fourth gym, when you enter Hassel will approach you with a new character Rika . They explain that they are members of the Elite Four , and that they’ve been keeping an eye on your progress. They will leave and you are then free to approach the Gym reception and challenge Kofu. Of course remember to put your best Pokémon at the front of your party before you begin.

Kofu has three Pokémon between levels 29 and 30. He opens with Veluza which has Pluck to counter Grass-types, and his Wugtrio has Mud-Slap to counter Electric-types. Despite this, taking these two types into battle should be relatively safe. The Crabominable hits very hard though, so be careful.

Once you beat Kofu he will give you the Gym Badge , which allows Pokémon up to level 40 to obey you. He gives you the TM for Chilling Water , which is a great move that lowers your opponent’s Attack while dealing damage.

As soon as you finish with Kofu, Nemona will come meet you at the Gym. Don’t worry, she won’t battle you this time, but she will tell you how proud she is of your efforts. With that done we’re ready to take on the next Team Star base.

Both Larry the Gym Leader , and the Quaking Earth Titan are near Kofu and Cascarrafa , but we’re going to fly to the East first and level up a bit before taking them on. Fly to the Levincia (North) Pokémon Center , and you can follow the road West to get to Zapapico first. This will unlock some new fly points and be close to the Poison Crew's Base. It looks like you can travel to from the East Province (Area Two) Pokémon Center, but a sheer cliff will stop you from reaching Zapico.

Along the way we’ll be preparing for the next Team Star base so we want some Ground - or Psychic-type on the team. Steel-types are also a good choice as they are immune to being Poisoned and Poison-type moves. You can find Cufant and Varoom on this path, and if you didn’t catch the Titan Orthworm then you’ll have an opportunity to find a regular one here. Halfway down the path to Zapapico, you will see a woman under a tent on the right, use her to heal your Pokémon.

Zapapico isn’t a big town, but it’s an important one to get the fly point for. It provides access to Dalizapa Passage , and it is also where you will find the man/woman who trades 10 Bronzor Fragments/Sinistea Chips for the Auspicious Armor / Malicious Armor needed to evolve Charcadet into Armarouge / Ceruledge . They are standing next to a fountain, and have the text “Fancy a trade?”. There are also a few cafés and sandwich ingredient shops here, but there are no items exclusive to the town.

When you’re done, set your route for the Navi Squad's Base in Tagtree Thicket . The Pokémon North of here are around level 35, so they are a bit stronger than what we’ve faced so far. However, there are Tinkatuff and Espathra in this area, which can be decent counters to the Navi Squad's Poison Pokémon. Tagtree Thicket has a border around it that can only be crossed at certain points. You can walk or fly back to the woman who healed you along the path you came from, and head up the road to the North to get into the forest.

You’ll see a Pokémon Center right outside the thicket, which is a great place to heal. The entrance to the forest is marked with purple Team Star flags on either side. As you enter the Tagtree Thicket you’ll be entered into a cutscene. Clive will approach you and tell you that he has been keeping in contact with members of Team Star and wants to continue with Operation Starfall.

From here you can decide whether to go straight to the base, or to pick up some Pokémon from Tagtree Thicket. Scarlet players can pick up Oranguru here, which can be strong in the upcoming battles. Once you have caught everything you want, approach the front gates. You will see a Team Star Grunt arguing with a student who wants to go into the base and meet the leader Atticus . You approach the pair and tell them who you are. The Grunt will hurry inside, and Pokémon Trainer Youssef will fight you.

Youssef will try to overwhelm your team with Toxic and stalling strategies with Stockpile and Swallow . The Shroodle can be annoying with Flatter to confuse you, but overall it shouldn’t be too difficult. Once you beat Youssef, Clive will approach and talk to him. Cassiopeia then calls and tells you a little about Atticus and the Poison Squad. After this you are free to put your three Poison-type counters in the lead and head into the base.

Like with the other Team Star bases, you will have to defeat 30 Pokémon in Let’s Go battles within 10 minutes. You will commonly face Gastly , Haunter , Shroodle , Grafaiai , Paldean Wooper , and Clodsire , but Gulpin , Swalot , Seviper , Foongus , Amoonguss , Grimer , Venonat , and Venomoth can also appear. Don’t forget to heal at the vending machines if you need to.

Once that’s done you’re ready for the leader Atticus. He has three Pokémon and the Starmobile , and his Skuntank will prove an issue if you’re relying on Psychic-type attackers. Its mix of Toxic and Venoshock , which doubles in power when the opponent is Poisoned, is also devastating. Stench can flinch making this fight event more difficult if you don’t have speed on your side. The Muk is less threatening, though Sludge Wave hits hard, and Mud-Slap can be very disruptive. The Revavroom can be taken out with a single Ground-type move, but it hits very hard if you allow it to.

As with all Starmobile’s Atticus’ one is very strong with a lot of HP. It has Toxic Debris spreading Toxic Spikes around the field, preventing you from switching around too much. Its gimmick is all about Speed . Spin Out will sharply lower its Speed, and Flame Charge will raise it. However, even if its Speed is lowered it still has a good chance at outspeeding your team.

Once you’ve defeated Atticus, you’ll see one of his memories where he shows his face. It shows Atticus giving the Team Star leaders their outfits after he has designed and made them. The memory explains how Atticus was bullied for his love of fashion, which is why he found a home with Team Star. They also talk about how they want to train and become better at battling. Atticus will then take a picture with you for defeating him and gives you TM102 Gunk Shot , a powerful physical Poison-type move.

Clive brings over Youssef, the student that you defeated at the gate, to talk to Atticus. The student expresses gratitude to Atticus and Team Star for pushing the bullies out of the school. Atticus explains that the big boss of Team Star has since gone missing, and that the leaders will defend their bases until their boss returns. He also explains that the boss is a recluse, and none of the members of Team Star have actually met them.

Once outside the base Cassiopeia will call you again. Cassiopeia explains that the main goal of Operation Starfall is to take down the big boss, the person who formed Team Star. However, like Atticus, they don’t know who the big boss is. Despite this they believe that the big boss will make themselves known once all five bases are taken down. Cassiopeia then transfers you 7,000 LP, upgrades the TM machine, and Penny stops by with plenty of Pokémon materials. Koraidon / Miraidon will pop out of its ball and give her a fright, and she will explain that taking down the big boss is important to her too.
After this cutscene you are free to travel to Medali and take on our next Gym Leader , Larry .

Our next stop is the Medali Gym , and while the town looks close to Cascarrafa , without the ability to climb it is easier to get there from Zapapico (West). Leaving Zapapico via this exit, and taking the fork to the right, will lead us on the path straight to Medali with a fly point we can unlock on the way. One thing to note is that the Pokémon here can be slightly higher level than what we’ve faced so far, coming in around the mid-30s. This is also the level of our Gym Leader Larry , so you’ll need to make sure your team is ready to take them on. Once you leave the tunnel head down the hill to enter Medali for the first time.

Medali has a lot of shops, but the most important one is Treasure Eatery . This is not only where you’ll face the next Gym Leader, but also where you go if you want to change your Pokémon’s Tera type . Be warned you’ll need 50 Tera Shards of the type you want to change to. You probably won’t have this many at this point unless you’ve been participating in a lot of Tera Raid Battles.

To begin the Medali Gym Test you’ll first have to enter the Gym. Once you do so Nemona will challenge you to another battle. However, you won’t fight her until after you have taken down Larry, so you don’t have to worry about her yet. When signing up to the Gym Test you are asked to find four clues as to Larry’s favorite food, and tell the code word to the wait staff at the Treasure Eatery.

You can find these by battling trainers around town. They will then give you a location where you can find the clue. You can skip all of this by going straight to the waiter if you know the order, but you will miss out on the money and experience. There is one trainer in front of the restaurant, one in front of Sure Cans, and one in front of the amphitheater. You will notice them as their speech bubbles are outlined in yellow.

One will tell you that they want some ice cream, leading you to Sugar-N-Ice near the Treasure Eatery where the odd food out is Grilled Rice Balls. The next will say to listen to the blue bird Pokémon, meaning the Squawkabilly that tells you “Medium”. The next will tell you to look for a dark spot surrounded by stairs, and you can find the words Fire Blast hidden behind the grate. Finally, ask the man eating at the counter, and he will tell you that regulars season their food with “Lemon”. All that’s left is to approach the waiter and ask for Grilled rice balls, Medium serving, Extra crispy Fire Blast style, and Lemon. You can then talk to the waiter again to challenge Larry.

Larry’s team isn’t too intimidating, except Staraptor which has Intimidate and can lower your Attack . Fighting-types are best here, and you’ll want to watch out for status moves like Yawn and Glare . Komala ’s Comatose , and Staraptor ’s Facade also mean that you don’t want to status Larry’s team back. Once you are done, you’ll grab a picture with Larry, and be given TM025 Facade, a strong Normal-type move that doubles in power when you are statused. Pokémon caught below level 45 will now always obey.

After you’ve finished against Larry, Geeta will approach. Nemona tells you a bit more about her, and how Geeta’s the Top Champion . Geeta says she’s here to scope out top talent, and Nemona will give you that battle she promised. Don’t worry, Geeta will heal your team before the battle starts. Nemona’s team is the same no matter her first partner Pokémon, except for that Pokémon. She will always Terastylize this Pokémon, but like our other fights with Nemona, it doesn’t matter if you win or lose.

Once you’re finished Geeta will give you a few TM171s . This is Tera Blast , a move that takes on a Pokémon’s Tera type when it’s Terstylized. It also adapts to your highest offensive stat, so it’s a great move to give your Pokémon more type coverage, particularly given that we’ve just unlocked the Treasure Eatery. If you don’t Terastylize then it is a fairly powerful Normal-type special move. After this Geeta will return you to Larry’s Gym and you are free to take on the next challenge.

Leaving Medali from the East will take you on a path towards Glaseado Mountain. Heading either directly North East or following a more winding path East, South and then North will take you to Montenevera and your next Gym Battle with Gym Leader Ryme . The snowy landscape of Glaseado Mountain is home to a variety of Ice-type Pokémon, catching one here might come in useful against one of the Elite Four later. 
The wild Pokémon you can encounter on Glaseado Mountain can range in level from the mid-30s to low-40s and cover an array of typings so avoid placing all your trust in a single Fire-type Pokémon. Ryme's level is at the top of this level range so be prepared for a step-up from Larry's mid-30s level Pokémon.
